messages:
prod-monitor-bot: [ALERT] spike detected: /v1/generate 5xx rate 18% over 1m in us-west-2, p95 latency 1.8s. paging oncall.

oncall-bot: Paging caroline (oncall). Escalation: level 1. Paging via PD.

caroline: ack, seeing alerts. grabbing dashboards now. first thought: sudden queue growth on scheduler-batcher.

lee: looking at batcher-queue length -> tail is growing, head-of-line latched on a few runaway requests. Qlen jumped from ~200 -> 4.2k in 30s.

samir: logs show a pattern of big requests with long token lengths that bypass prefix cache. looks like a client spike hitting long-seq workloads.

caroline: can we throttle incoming long-seq traffic or drop to smaller batch windows? trying quick mitigations: set batching.max_window_ms=20, enable preemptive-evict.

lee: runbook step: reduce batch window and enable permissive-eviction on scheduler. hitting the cluster with the following patch now.

lee: ```json
{
  "scheduler": {
    "batch_window_ms": 20,
    "eviction_policy": "preemptive"
  }
}
```

prod-monitor-bot: Config change applied to fleet-ow1 in 38s, rolling to 12 nodes.

caroline: also toggling fallback-route to warm-model-pool (lower capacity but simpler runtime) to relieve sat nodes.

samir: while that rolls, we should open a hard-cap on request token-length at the gateway to avoid new long jobs. can do an immediate nginx rewrite: `if ($content_length > 20000) return 413;`

maria: on support side, we're seeing increased inbound tickets from large customers - tagging high-impact orgs: AcmeGames, DocuParse. ops, any ETA on visible customer impact?

helpdesk-bot: 2 active customer tickets elevated to P1: AcmeGames (timeouts), DocuParse (5xx). Added to this thread.

lee: metrics: after batch-window reduction, queue length down to ~900 after first wave, 5xx rate dropped to 9% (from 18%). still above baseline. rolling fallback helped a bit — warm pool now handling ~22% of traffic.

caroline: good. next step: throttle burst traffic at gateway for users matching long-seq UA. pushing a temporary rule to weight-routes for /v1/generate: limit concurrency per IP to 8.

samir: sample logs attached: ```
[2026-03-15T10:12:05Z] request_id=abc123 model=llama-13b tokens=12000 queue_ms=4200
[2026-03-15T10:12:07Z] request_id=def456 model=llama-13b tokens=9800 queue_ms=3900
```

caroline: moving to handoff in ~10m. Lee, Samir — please prepare a short summary for next oncall (maria). Include mitigations attempted and metrics.

lee: summary drafted: batch window -> 20ms, eviction preemptive ON, fallback routing to warm pool, gateway token-length cap for new requests, temporary per-IP concurrency cap=8.

maria: taking handoff. I need current customer-impact estimate and any outstanding mitigations.

caroline: current estimate: peak impacted traffic ~14% of global /v1/generate requests in us-west-2, sustained errors affecting 8% of requests after first mitigations. Two high-value customers experiencing timeouts.

maria: I'll keep fallback routing and eviction policy active, and coordinate with capacity team to spin up 6 extra warm nodes if needed. please document exact node IDs and config diffs.

samir: I've added an alert rule to suppress noisy long-seq clients once the gateway cap is active. also turned on token-length telemetry for the next 30m.

caroline: quick note — we observed one scheduler process repeatedly locking on KV cache eviction; suspect kernel-level GC on that host. flagged node: ow1-12. taken out of rotation.

lee: node ow1-12 removed, traffic drained. scheduler on ow1-15 took over shards.

prod-monitor-bot: 5xx rate now 3.1% over 1m, queue length stable ~120. p95 latency 480ms.

maria: customer impact reduced, support update queued. going to inform AcmeGames and DocuParse that we're mitigating and will follow up with RCA.

helpdesk-bot: Draft sent to AcmeGames: "We've mitigated the surge and applied temporary throttles; engineering is working on a permanent fix."

caroline: action items for postmortem: 1) tune default batch window rules for long-seq workloads, 2) add circuit-breaker in gateway for token-length spikes, 3) automate fallback routing when queue qlen > X, 4) investigate ow1-12 kernel GC interaction with KV eviction.

maria: agreed. I'll own follow-up 4 and 3. Samir pls own 2. Caroline own 1. Lee to verify new runbook steps.

samir: one more note — plan to add per-model max_tokens cap and soft-fail with 429 for large requests instead of letting them pile up. drafting proposal.

prod-monitor-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. 5xx 1m < 5%. No new P1 tickets in last 15m.

caroline: closing phone bridge. if metrics regress, re-open and escalate. great job team :thumbsup:

maria: taking postmortem ownership. Will schedule RCA and ping this channel when done.

helpdesk-bot: Support: tickets updated, customers notified.

oncall-bot: Incident logged: incident-2026-03-15-3249995555. Severity: Sev2. Handoff complete.

caroline: thread archived for RCA notes.
